quantity.quote: New data are reported from the operation of a 4.0 kg CF$_{3}$I bubble chamber in the 6800-foot-deep SNOLAB underground laboratory.
Twenty single nuclear recoil event candidates and three multiple bubble events were observed during a total exposure of 553 kg-days distributed over three different bubble nucleation thresholds.
The 6800-foot (6010 m water equivalent) overburden of the SNOLAB site eliminates neutrons of cosmogenic origin.
with a lower bound of $>$99.3% rejection of alpha-decay events

Also called the 'two-liter' chamber in the title of arXiv:1008.3518 (3.5 kg of CF3I). The Fustin dissertation (arXiv:2401.07384, written March 2012) is a thesis posted to arXiv in 2024 and is cited as a source for the chamber's history.
The 60 kg chamber of the COUPP programme is recorded as experiment:pico-60 (alias COUPP-60), not here.

physics_goals.quote: The Chicagoland Observatory for Underground Particle Physics (COUPP) employs the bubble chamber technique to search for WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering [4].
physics_goals.value: WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering, spin-dependent and spin-independent, with superheated CF3I

summary.plain: COUPP-4kg was a two-litre bubble chamber of superheated CF3I, first run in a Fermilab tunnel and then two kilometres underground at SNOLAB. Its papers report world-best limits on how strongly heavy dark matter could couple to nuclear spin.
summary.technical: 2-litre CF3I bubble chamber with acoustic alpha/nuclear-recoil discrimination (alpha rejection >99.3%): 3.5 kg run in the MINOS near-detector tunnel at Fermilab (19 Aug-18 Dec 2009, 28.1 kg-days), then a 4.0 kg run in the SNOLAB J-Drift (Sept 2010-Aug 2011; 553 kg-days over three thresholds; 20 single-recoil candidates, with an internal neutron background estimated to account for five). A second SNOLAB run followed in 2012. The synthetic fused-silica jar sits in the pressure vessel of COUPP-2kg.
